records.literal_gloss: For the director, to the flutes. A psalm of David.

en.L: For the director: for the flutes. A psalm of David.
en.B: For the music director. For flutes. A psalm of David.
en.R: For the leader of the music. To be played on flutes. A song of David.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : pour les flûtes. Un psaume de David.
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Pour flûtes. Un psaume de David.
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. À jouer sur des flûtes. Un chant de David.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: As in Psalm 3, the title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
alternatives: for the end (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: the flutes: an instrument or a tune
alternatives: a tune called 'Inheritances' (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The word (nechilot) occurs only here. It is usually linked with the word for a flute (chalil), so the psalm would be accompanied by flutes; it may instead be the name of a tune. The ancient Greek translation read it as "inheritances".

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1, Readable says what a psalm is.

records.literal_gloss: My words give ear to, YHWH; consider my sighing.

en.L: To my words give ear, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; perceive my sighing.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, hear what I say; take note of my sighs.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, please listen to what I am saying. Pay attention to my quiet groans.

fr.L: À mes paroles prête l’oreille, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; discerne mon soupir.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, écoute ce que je dis ; prête attention à mes soupirs.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, écoute ce que je dis. Fais attention à mes plaintes murmurées.

decisions.choice: sighing: a low groan or murmured prayer
decisions.reason: The word (hagig) is related to the verb for murmuring in 1:2 (hagah). It is the half-spoken prayer or groan of someone in trouble; Psalm 39:4 uses it for brooding thought.

decisions.choice: give ear, consider: three requests to be heard
decisions.reason: Verses 2-3 ask three times to be heard (give ear, consider, pay attention), a common way to open a prayer for help (Psalm 17:1).

decisions.choice: give ear
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for ear; Literal shows the picture.

source.text: הַקְשִׁ֤יבָה׀לְק֬וֹל שַׁוְעִ֗י מַלְכִּ֥י וֵאלֹהָ֑י כִּֽי־אֵ֝לֶ֗יךָ אֶתְפַּלָּֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Attend to the sound of my cry for help, my king and my God, for to you I pray.

en.L: Pay attention to the sound of my cry for help, my King and my God, for to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I pray.
en.B: Listen to me crying for help, my King and my God, because it is to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that I pray.
en.R: Hear me as I call for help, my King and my God. I am praying to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: Sois attentif au son de mon cri au secours, mon Roi et mon Dieu, car vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} je prie.
fr.B: Écoute-moi crier au secours, mon Roi et mon Dieu, car c’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que je prie.
fr.R: Entends-moi quand j’appelle au secours, mon Roi et mon Dieu. C’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} que je prie.

decisions.choice: my King and my God: the king's own King
decisions.reason: David, Israel's king, calls the LORD his King. The LORD is the true king of his people (1 Samuel 8:7; Psalm 24:7-10), and the human king rules under him.

decisions.choice: cry for help: a shout for rescue
decisions.reason: The word (shav'a) is a call for help in trouble (Exodus 2:23).

decisions.choice: King (capitalized)
decisions.reason: "King" is capitalized as a title of God, as "Lord" is.

source.text: יְֽהוָ֗ה בֹּ֭קֶרתִּשְׁמַ֣ע קוֹלִ֑י בֹּ֥קֶר אֶֽעֱרָךְ־לְ֝ךָ֗ וַאֲצַפֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH, [in the] morning you hear my voice; [in the] morning I arrange for you and watch.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, [in the] morning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear my voice; [in the] morning I set [it] out before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and keep watch.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, at daybreak {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear my voice. At daybreak I set everything out before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and keep watch.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, every morning {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hear me. Every morning I bring my requests to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and wait for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to answer.

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, [au] matin {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} entends ma voix ; [au] matin je [la] dispose devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} et je guette.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, dès l’aube {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} entends ma voix. Dès l’aube je prépare tout devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} et je reste aux aguets.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, chaque matin {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’entends. Chaque matin je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} présente mes demandes et j’attends que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} répondes.

decisions.choice: I arrange: I set out my prayer, or my sacrifice
decisions.reason: The verb ('arak) means to set in order. It is used of laying out a sacrifice on the altar (Leviticus 1:7-8) and of setting out a case in court (Job 23:4). Here it has no object, so it may be either, or a prayer offered like a morning sacrifice.

decisions.choice: keep watch: look out for an answer
decisions.reason: The verb (tsafah) is used of a lookout on a wall. Habakkuk 2:1 uses it of watching to see what the LORD will answer.

decisions.choice: morning: the time of the morning sacrifice and of help
decisions.reason: The day began with the morning offering (Exodus 29:39), and the morning is often the time when God's help comes (Psalm 46:6).

decisions.choice: bring my requests; wait for you to answer
decisions.reason: Readable takes the verb as prayer (m1) and says what the watching is for (m2).

source.text: כִּ֤י׀לֹ֤א אֵֽל־חָפֵ֘ץ רֶ֥שַׁע׀אָ֑תָּה לֹ֖א יְגֻרְךָ֣ רָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: For not a God delighting [in] wickedness [are] you; not will sojourn with you evil.

en.L: For not a God delighting [in] wickedness [are] {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; evil will not sojourn with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are not a God who takes pleasure in wickedness; evil cannot be {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} guest.
en.R: You are not a God who enjoys what is wicked. No evil person can live near {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: Car [{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’es] pas un Dieu qui se plaît à la méchanceté, {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; le mal ne séjournera pas chez {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} n’es pas un Dieu qui se plaît à la méchanceté ; le mal ne peut pas être {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} hôte.
fr.R: Tu n’es pas un Dieu qui aime ce qui est mauvais. Aucune personne mauvaise ne peut vivre près de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

decisions.choice: sojourn with you: stay as your guest
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) means to live somewhere as a guest or resident foreigner. Psalm 15:1 asks who may be a guest in the LORD's tent; evil may not.

decisions.choice: evil: evil, or an evil person
decisions.reason: The word (ra') can mean evil or an evil person; the next verses speak of evil people.

decisions.choice: No evil person
decisions.reason: Readable takes the word as a person (m2), as verse 6 continues.

source.text: לֹֽא־יִתְיַצְּב֣וּ הֽ֭וֹלְלִים לְנֶ֣גֶד עֵינֶ֑יךָ שָׂ֝נֵ֗אתָ כָּל־פֹּ֥עֲלֵי אָֽוֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: Not will take their stand [the] boasters before your eyes; you hate all doers of iniquity.

en.L: Boasters will not take their stand before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} eyes; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hate all workers of iniquity.
en.B: Those who boast cannot stand in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} sight; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hate all who practice evil.
en.R: Proud people cannot stand in front of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You hate everyone who does evil.

fr.L: Les vantards ne se tiendront pas devant {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} yeux ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} hais tous ceux qui pratiquent l’iniquité.
fr.B: Ceux qui se vantent ne peuvent pas tenir sous {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} regard ; {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} détestes tous ceux qui font le mal.
fr.R: Les orgueilleux ne peuvent pas se présenter devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Tu détestes tous ceux qui font le mal.

decisions.choice: take their stand: stand before God, or against him
decisions.reason: It is the verb of 2:2, where kings "take their stand" against the LORD. The boastful cannot present themselves before him, as a person stands before a king.

decisions.choice: boasters: the arrogant who brag
decisions.reason: The word (holelim) describes people who boast and act like fools in their pride (Psalm 73:3).

decisions.choice: you hate: God firmly rejects them
decisions.reason: God's hatred is not a passing feeling but his settled rejection of evil and of those who devote themselves to it. The psalm is not about personal dislike; it says who may come into God's presence.

source.text: תְּאַבֵּד֮ דֹּבְרֵ֪י כָ֫זָ֥ב אִישׁ־דָּמִ֥ים וּמִרְמָ֗ה יְתָ֘עֵ֥ב׀יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: You destroy speakers of falsehood; [a] man of blood and deceit YHWH abhors.

en.L: You destroy speakers of lies; {{gender:a person|a man}} of bloodshed and deceit {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} abhors.
en.B: You bring liars to ruin. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} loathes those who shed blood and deceive.
en.R: You destroy people who lie. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} hates people who kill and trick others.

fr.L: Tu fais périr ceux qui disent le mensonge ; {{gender:la personne|l’homme}} de sang et de fraude, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a en horreur.
fr.B: Tu mènes les menteurs à leur perte. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a en horreur ceux qui versent le sang et qui trompent.
fr.R: Tu détruis les gens qui mentent. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} déteste ceux qui tuent et qui trompent les autres.

decisions.choice: man of blood: someone who sheds blood, a violent person
decisions.reason: A "man of blood" is a murderer or a violent person (2 Samuel 16:7). Deceit (mirmah) is the trickery that goes with it.

decisions.choice: the LORD abhors: from "you" to "the LORD"
decisions.reason: The psalmist speaks to God ("you destroy") and then about him ("the LORD"), a shift common in the Psalms.

decisions.choice: a person, with "a man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The phrase describes anyone who is violent and deceitful, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording; Balanced and Readable say "those" and "people".

source.text: וַאֲנִ֗י בְּרֹ֣ב חַ֭סְדְּךָ אָב֣וֹא בֵיתֶ֑ךָ אֶשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֥ה אֶל־הֵֽיכַל־קָ֝דְשְׁךָ֗ בְּיִרְאָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: But I, in [the] abundance of your loyal love, will enter your house; I will bow down toward [the] temple of your holiness in fear of you.

en.L: But I, in [the] abundance of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, will enter {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house; I will bow down toward [the] temple of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holiness in fear of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: But I, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love is so great, will come into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house; in awe of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I will bow down toward {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy temple.
en.R: But because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} love is so great and so faithful, I will come into {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} house. I will bow down toward {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy temple, full of respect for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: Mais moi, dans [l’]abondance de {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} amour loyal, j’entrerai dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} maison ; je me prosternerai vers [le] temple de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sainteté dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} crainte.
fr.B: Mais moi, parce que {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} amour fidèle est si grand, j’entrerai dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} maison ; rempli de respect pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, je me prosternerai vers {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} saint temple.
fr.R: Mais parce que {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} amour est si grand et si fidèle, j’entrerai dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} maison. Je me prosternerai vers {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} temple saint, plein de respect pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

decisions.choice: loyal love: love that keeps faith
decisions.reason: The word (chesed) is love that stays loyal to a relationship and a promise: the LORD's love for his people, "abounding in loyal love and faithfulness" (Exodus 34:6). The faithful one of 4:4 (chasid) is a person who shows the same loyalty.

decisions.choice: But I, in the abundance of your loyal love: only by God's love
decisions.reason: The psalmist sets himself apart from the boasters who cannot stand before God, but he comes in only because of God's great love, not because of his own goodness.

decisions.choice: your house, your holy temple: the place of worship
decisions.reason: The house and temple (hekal, a palace or temple) are where the LORD is worshiped. In David's time this was the tent that housed the ark (2 Samuel 6:17); the tent at Shiloh is also called a temple (1 Samuel 1:9; 3:3).

decisions.choice: loyal love
decisions.reason: "Loyal love" says both that it is love and that it keeps faith (m1). Readable says "so great and so faithful".

decisions.choice: in awe of you
decisions.reason: The fear is reverence (as in 2:11); Literal keeps "fear".

decisions.choice: ḥesed: "amour loyal" (Literal), "amour fidèle" (Balanced, Readable), for this block of psalms
decisions.reason: The word is love that keeps faith with a commitment (m1). "Bonté" and "miséricorde" say only part of it. Literal pairs the noun with "loyal" as the English does; Balanced and Readable use the more natural "fidèle".

source.text: יְהוָ֤ה׀נְחֵ֬נִי בְצִדְקָתֶ֗ךָ לְמַ֥עַן שׁוֹרְרָ֑י הַיְשַׁ֖ר לְפָנַ֣י דַּרְכֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH, lead me in your righteousness because of those watching me; make straight before me your way.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, lead me in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness because of those who watch me; make straight before me {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, guide me in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness, because my enemies are watching; level {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} road in front of me.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, my enemies are watching for me to fall. Lead me in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} right ways. Make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} path straight and clear in front of me.

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, conduis-moi dans {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} justice à cause de ceux qui me guettent ; aplanis devant moi {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, guide-moi par {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} justice, car mes ennemis m’épient ; rends {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} route bien droite devant moi.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, mes ennemis attendent que je tombe. Conduis-moi sur {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} chemins justes. Rends {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin droit et dégagé devant moi.

decisions.choice: those watching me: enemies lying in wait
decisions.reason: The word (shorer) is used for enemies who watch closely for a chance to attack (Psalm 27:11; 56:3).

decisions.choice: in your righteousness: as you are righteous
decisions.reason: The LORD's righteousness is his faithfulness to do what is right; the psalmist asks to be led by it, in the right path he provides.

decisions.choice: make straight: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: Here the Hebrew text writes one form of the verb and its notes say to read another. The difference is only of form; both mean "make straight". The words follow the form to be read.

decisions.choice: watching for me to fall
decisions.reason: Readable says what the enemies are watching for (m1).

source.text: כִּ֤י אֵ֪ין בְּפִ֡יהוּ נְכוֹנָה֮ קִרְבָּ֪ם הַ֫וּ֥וֹת קֶֽבֶר־פָּת֥וּחַ גְּרוֹנָ֑ם לְ֝שׁוֹנָ֗ם יַחֲלִֽיקוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: For there is not in his mouth [anything] reliable; their inward part [is] destruction; an open grave [is] their throat; their tongue they make smooth.

en.L: For there is nothing reliable in their mouth; their inner self [is] destruction; an open grave [is] their throat; their tongue they make smooth.
en.B: Not one thing they say is reliable; deep inside them is only ruin. Their throats are graves left open, and their tongues are smooth with flattery.
en.R: You cannot trust anything they say. Inside, they only want to destroy. What comes out of their mouths is deadly, like an open grave. They say nice things they do not mean.

fr.L: Car il n’y a rien de sûr dans leur bouche ; leur intérieur [est] ruine ; un tombeau ouvert [est] leur gosier ; leur langue, ils [la] rendent lisse.
fr.B: Rien de ce qu’ils disent n’est sûr ; au fond d’eux il n’y a que ruine. Leur gorge est une tombe ouverte, et leur langue est douce de flatteries.
fr.R: On ne peut se fier à rien de ce qu’ils disent. Au fond, ils ne veulent que détruire. Ce qui sort de leur bouche est mortel, comme une tombe ouverte. Ils disent des choses gentilles qu’ils ne pensent pas.

decisions.choice: his mouth: the mouth of each of them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "his mouth", speaking of each enemy, and then "their" for the rest of the verse.

decisions.choice: destruction: ruin, malice
decisions.reason: The word (havvot) means ruin or disaster; what fills them inside is the wish to destroy.

decisions.choice: an open grave is their throat: their words bring death
decisions.reason: An open grave is ready to swallow the dead; their speech is deadly. Paul quotes this line and the next, with others, to show that all have sinned (Romans 3:13).

decisions.choice: they make their tongue smooth: they flatter
decisions.reason: A smooth tongue is flattery, pleasant words that hide harm (Proverbs 29:5).

decisions.choice: their mouth (L); they say (B, R)
decisions.reason: The text means each of them (m1), so every level says "their" or "they".

source.text: הַֽאֲשִׁימֵ֨ם׀אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים יִפְּלוּ֮ מִֽמֹּעֲצ֪וֹתֵ֫יהֶ֥ם בְּרֹ֣ב פִּ֭שְׁעֵיהֶם הַדִּיחֵ֑מוֹ כִּי־מָ֥רוּ בָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Hold them guilty, God; may they fall by their schemes; for the multitude of their transgressions drive them out, for they have rebelled against you.

en.L: Hold them guilty, God; let them fall by their own counsels; for the multitude of their transgressions thrust them out, for they have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: Hold them to account, God! Let them be tripped up by their own schemes. Thrust them away for all their many crimes, since it is against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} that they have rebelled.
en.R: God, make them pay for what they have done! Let their own evil plans make them fall. Push them away because they have sinned so many times. They have turned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: Déclare-les coupables, Dieu ; qu’ils tombent par leurs propres desseins ; pour la multitude de leurs transgressions, chasse-les, car ils se sont rebellés contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.B: Fais-leur rendre des comptes, Dieu ! Qu’ils soient pris au piège de leurs propres complots. Rejette-les pour leurs crimes si nombreux, puisque c’est contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qu’ils se sont révoltés.
fr.R: Dieu, fais-leur payer ce qu’ils ont fait ! Que leurs propres plans mauvais les fassent tomber. Repousse-les, parce qu’ils ont péché tant de fois. Ils se sont tournés contre {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

decisions.choice: hold them guilty: declare them guilty and let them bear it
decisions.reason: The verb ('asham) means to be guilty or to bear the penalty of guilt; here God is asked to treat them as guilty.

decisions.choice: a prayer for judgment on enemies
decisions.reason: Many psalms ask God to judge the wicked. The psalmist does not take revenge himself but leaves it to God, and he asks for a just judgment: that their own schemes bring them down. The reason given is that they have rebelled against God.

decisions.choice: transgressions, rebelled: open revolt against God
decisions.reason: Transgression (pesha') is rebellion, breaking faith with a ruler; "rebelled" (marah) says the same. Their sin is against God, not only against David.

decisions.choice: make them pay for what they have done
decisions.reason: Readable says what holding them guilty means (m1).

source.text: וְיִשְׂמְח֨וּ כָל־ח֪וֹסֵי בָ֡ךְ לְעוֹלָ֣ם יְ֭רַנֵּנוּ וְתָסֵ֣ךְ עָלֵ֑ימוֹ וְֽיַעְלְצ֥וּ בְ֝ךָ֗ אֹהֲבֵ֥י שְׁמֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And let all who take refuge in you rejoice; forever let them shout for joy, and may you shelter them, and let those who love your name exult in you.

en.L: But let all who take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} rejoice; forever let them shout for joy; and may {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} shelter them, and let those who love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name exult in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: But let everyone who makes {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} their refuge be glad and sing for joy forever. Keep them under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} cover, and those who love {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name will find their joy in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: But let everyone who runs to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for safety be glad. Let them sing for joy forever. Protect them, so that those who love {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will be happy because of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: Mais que se réjouissent tous ceux qui se réfugient en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; pour toujours, qu’ils crient de joie ; et puisses-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les abriter, et qu’exultent en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ceux qui aiment {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom !
fr.B: Mais que tous ceux qui font de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} leur refuge soient dans la joie et chantent de bonheur pour toujours. Garde-les à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} abri, et ceux qui aiment {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} nom trouveront leur joie en {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.
fr.R: Mais que tous ceux qui courent se mettre à l’abri auprès de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} soient heureux. Qu’ils chantent de joie pour toujours. Protège-les, pour que ceux qui {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}aiment soient heureux grâce à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.

decisions.choice: take refuge: seek shelter in God
decisions.reason: The verb (chasah) is the one that closes Psalm 2 (2:12): to run to someone for shelter.

decisions.choice: shelter them: cover them with protection
decisions.reason: The verb (sakak) means to screen or cover over, as wings cover (Exodus 25:20). It may be a request, "cover them", or a promise, "you will cover them".

decisions.choice: your name: God himself as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: The LORD's name stands for who he is and what he has shown himself to be (Exodus 3:15; 34:5-7). To love his name is to love him.

decisions.choice: those who love you
decisions.reason: Readable says what loving the name means (m3).

decisions.choice: makes you their refuge (B); runs to you for safety (R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:12.

source.text: כִּֽי־אַתָּה֮ תְּבָרֵ֪ךְ צַ֫דִּ֥יק יְהוָ֑ה כַּ֝צִּנָּ֗ה רָצ֥וֹן תַּעְטְרֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For you bless [the] righteous, YHWH; like the shield, [with] favor you surround him.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bless [the] righteous, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; like the large shield, [with] favor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} surround {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} bless the righteous, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}; {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} favor surrounds them like a great shield.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} always bless people who do what is right. Your kindness protects them on every side, like a big shield.

fr.L: Car {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} bénis [le] juste, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; comme le grand bouclier, [de] faveur {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’entoures.
fr.B: Car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} bénis le juste, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} faveur l’entoure comme un grand bouclier.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} bénis toujours ceux qui font ce qui est juste. Ta bonté les protège de tous côtés, comme un grand bouclier.

decisions.choice: the large shield: a shield that covers the whole body
decisions.reason: This shield (tsinnah) is the large one, carried before a soldier (1 Samuel 17:7), not the small round shield of 3:4. God's favor covers the righteous from head to foot.

decisions.choice: favor: God's goodwill and acceptance
decisions.reason: Favor (ratson) is the goodwill of someone who accepts and delights in another (Proverbs 8:35).

decisions.choice: the righteous, him: anyone who is righteous
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of "the righteous" and "him" as one person who stands for all of them, as in 1:6.

decisions.choice: the righteous ... them (B); people who do what is right ... them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for the righteous as a group (m3); Literal follows the gender setting.
